title: Agentic AI Insurance Proposal Editor | CopyCat
summary: Ask AI to edit your insurance proposal end to end. See CopyCat’s agentic editor, example requests, review checklist, and connected insurance workflows.
body_markdown:
The short version


- CopyCat’s new agentic editor carries out requested changes inside an insurance proposal, end to end.
- Describe the edit in plain language, review the updated document, and make any finishing changes before export.
- Proposals sit alongside quote comparison, renewal review, policy checking, contract review, and employee benefits workflows.


The first draft is only part of an insurance proposal. Before it goes to the client, someone still needs to refine the opening, explain the recommendation, and make the next steps clear. CopyCat’s new agentic AI editor brings that work into the proposal itself: tell it what you want changed and it carries out the edit for you.


The release extends our[insurance proposal builder](https://www.runcopycat.com/insurance-proposal-software) . Start with carrier documents, generate a proposal in your agency’s format, then work with AI to refine it. You can also edit directly. Your team reviews the finished document before it reaches the client.


## What is an agentic insurance proposal editor?


An agentic proposal editor takes an instruction and applies the requested change to the proposal. In CopyCat, that means AI can perform the document edit end to end within the proposal workspace. The useful question is simple: did the document change the way you intended, and is the result ready for your review?


A request might be to simplify the recommendation, shorten an opening, or add a next-steps section. Give the editor the audience, the section to change, and any details it should preserve. Coverage facts still need to agree with the source documents, and the recommendation still needs the broker’s judgment.


## What can you ask AI to edit?


Use these illustrative requests as starting points when trying the editor on your own proposal.


Example request What to check afterward


Rewrite the opening for a business owner who does not work in insurance. Keep it to two sentences. The opening is clearer and still describes the proposed coverage accurately.


Make the recommendation easier to understand. Preserve the carrier names, premiums, and limits. The explanation is useful, and material values still match the carrier documents.


Add a next-steps section using these outstanding items: signed application and updated statement of values. The section contains the supplied items and introduces no unsupported requirements.


Shorten this section while keeping the deductible explanation. The shorter version retains the information the client needs to assess the tradeoff.


Specific instructions make the result easier to evaluate. If a change depends on a revised quote, use the correct document and verify the affected values. A writing instruction should never become an assumption about coverage.


## From carrier quote to reviewed proposal


1. Start with the account documents and your[agency’s proposal template](https://www.runcopycat.com/insurance-proposal-template) . Include the relevant quotes and supporting files.
2. Generate the proposal and review the coverage details against their sources.
3. Tell the agentic editor which section to change, what you want it to accomplish, and what must stay intact.
4. Review the applied edit in the document. Check the recommendation, material values, and any affected sections.
5. Make final adjustments, confirm the client-facing output, and export the proposal.


Evaluate the whole task, including review and corrections. A useful demo starts with your account packet, includes a real revision request, and ends with a proposal your team would be comfortable sharing. You can[see the proposal editor preview](https://www.runcopycat.com/insurance-proposal-software#proposal-workspace) or[explore sample proposals](https://www.runcopycat.com/insurance-proposal-examples) before a walkthrough.


## One proposal, connected to the rest of the account work


Proposal editing is one part of CopyCat. Each app handles a different question in the account lifecycle. Choose the workflow for the job in front of you:


CopyCat app The job it helps you finish


[Proposals and agentic editing](https://www.runcopycat.com/insurance-proposal-software) Turn carrier quotes into your branded proposal, ask AI to apply edits, and review the finished recommendation.


[Quote comparison](https://www.runcopycat.com/insurance-quote-comparison-software) Compare competing carrier options with source references for the differences.


[Renewal review](https://www.runcopycat.com/commercial-renewal-comparison-software) Compare expiring and renewal terms and investigate changes before the client decides.


[Policy checking](https://www.runcopycat.com/commercial-insurance-policy-checking-software) Check issued policy documents against the approved placement and flag discrepancies for follow-up.

Those workflows answer different questions. A renewal comparison explains what changed between policy periods. Policy checking asks whether the issued coverage matches the expected placement. Contract review asks whether supplied evidence supports a contractual requirement. Keep the review focused on the question, then use the proposal to explain the recommendation to the client.


## How to evaluate CopyCat alongside Outmarket, Fulcrum, and Cooper AI


CopyCat publishes this guide. The vendor descriptions below reflect public product materials reviewed September 19, 2026, not a hands-on benchmark or an independent ranking.


[Outmarket’s proposal builder](https://outmarket.ai/platform/proposal-builder) advertises rich-text editing, design controls, source citations, and version history.[Fulcrum](https://www.withfulcrum.com/) positions its platform around connected sales and servicing workflows.[Cooper’s retail-agency page](https://www.askcooper.ai/product/retail-agencies) describes submissions, system updates, renewal comparisons, and certificate workflows. These are overlapping products; a feature name alone will not settle the decision.


Ask each vendor to perform the same revision on the same permitted account documents. Watch where the edit happens, what the reviewer needs to verify, and how much work remains before the output is useful. Confirm integrations, implementation requirements, support, and pricing directly with each vendor.


Demo check Evidence to record


Applied edit The request, the original section, and the resulting document change.


Source fidelity Whether carrier names, premiums, limits, and qualifications remain correct.


Review effort Minutes spent checking and correcting the output, including failed attempts.


Agency format Whether the final export retains the required branding, tables, and sections.


Workflow fit Any manual transfers or additional systems needed to finish the task.


## Frequently asked questions


### Does the AI editor make changes inside the proposal?


Yes. CopyCat’s agentic editor applies the requested edits in the proposal. Review the updated document and make any additional changes before exporting.


### Can I still edit the proposal myself?


Yes. Direct document editing remains available alongside AI editing. Use whichever fits the change you need to make.


### Does end-to-end editing mean the proposal is sent automatically?


End-to-end describes carrying out the requested document edit. The workflow described here ends with your team reviewing the proposal before sharing it.


### How should I try it?


Bring a representative quote packet, your proposal format, and a revision you regularly make. Ask to see the complete path from generation through editing and final review.
